talking_points.headline: S&P: Hong Kong insurers to keep growing 8-10% despite Beijing's new offshore tax bite
talking_points.context_html: Following the Beijing offshore-insurance-tax shock we covered on 10 August — which knocked up to 7% off HSBC's London-listed shares — S&P Global Ratings now projects Hong Kong life insurers will still grow premiums 8-10% annually over the next two years, versus 33.7% last year, confirming a repricing rather than a structural break. Hong Kong has also reappointed Clement Cheung Wan-ching, Chief Executive of the Insurance Authority, for a further three years, giving the sector regulatory continuity as HSBC's own insurance arm absorbs the tax shift. For Adam, this is the first hard data point on how durable mainland demand for HK insurance really is post-tax, directly informing the growth assumptions behind WPB's wealth-division targets.
source_links: HK insurers to weather tax shift: S&P

talking_points.headline: Pictet tells clients to cut US dollar exposure — and they're not the only ones
talking_points.context_html: Kelvin Tay, Chief Investment Officer Asia at Pictet Wealth Management, and Frederik Ducrozet, Head of Strategy and Macroeconomic Research at Pictet, are urging clients to cut US Treasury and dollar exposure over the next decade on structural inflation and deficit concerns, favouring commodities and emerging-market equities instead. The call isn't isolated — a UBS survey already found nearly a third of family offices serving the ultra-wealthy have cut or plan to cut USD allocations, making this a live positioning debate HSBC's own CIO desk and RM-facing advisory content need a house view on before clients ask first.
source_links: Pictet warns on US asset exposure

talking_points.headline: China's rookie fund managers get an early, brutal lesson in AI-driven market risk
talking_points.context_html: A wave of newly-appointed Chinese fund managers handed outsized mandates saw portfolios fall 30%+ after June's AI-stock correction exposed crowded factor trades and heavy tech concentration, with one manager's two debut funds tumbling 33-36% in seven weeks. It's a live cautionary case as private banks — HSBC included — lean harder on AI for portfolio construction and advice: concentrated, correlated AI bets can unwind fast, and the same crowding risk applies to any AI-weighted model portfolio WPB pushes to clients.
source_links: China's young fund managers hit by AI sell-off

Regulatory & Markets.title: Hong Kong insurers to weather Beijing's tax shift with 8-10% premium growth: S&P
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Following the Beijing offshore-insurance-tax shock reported 10 August, S&P Global Ratings projects Hong Kong life insurers will still grow premiums 8-10% annually over the next two years despite the mainland's new 20% tax on offshore policy returns, down from 33.7% growth last year. S&P says underlying demand for multi-currency diversification and offshore wealth management remains intact, directly relevant to HSBC's insurance arm.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Hong Kong to reappoint insurance regulator as industry braces for tough period
Regulatory & Markets.summary: Hong Kong has reappointed Clement Cheung Wan-ching as Insurance Authority CEO for a further three-year term from 15 August 2026, as the sector navigates Beijing's new offshore-tax enforcement and slowing premium growth. Continuity at the regulator signals Hong Kong's intent to defend its position as an offshore wealth and insurance hub.
